claims.claim: In G(n,p), every possible edge is included independently with probability p; in G(n,m), the edge count is fixed.
claims.locator: Erdős and Rényi, On random graphs I (1959); independent-edge and fixed-edge-count models

claims.claim: For G(n,p), expected edge count is p n(n−1)/2 and expected degree is p(n−1).
claims.locator: Durrett, Random Graph Dynamics, Chapter 2; linearity of expectation over independent edge indicators

claims.claim: For p=c/n, the giant-component threshold is at c=1 (equivalently p of order 1/n).
claims.locator: Park (2023), §2, Theorem 2.2; Threshold Phenomena for Random Discrete Structures

claims.claim: The full-graph connectivity threshold is of order (ln n)/n, distinct from the giant-component threshold.
claims.locator: Durrett, Random Graph Dynamics, §2.8, Threshold for connectivity

claims.claim: The binomial degree distribution approaches a Poisson distribution in the sparse large-n regime with bounded expected degree.
claims.locator: Durrett, Random Graph Dynamics, Chapter 2; Binomial(n−1,p) degree with p=λ/n
